thread:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert at 23:07 UTC - canary lane showing 502 errors and image digest drift. automatic health check flagged 2/10 canaries failing.

incident-bot: Paging anna (oncall). severity: high for canary rollout, potential user impact isolated to 10% traffic.

anna (oncall): I got it, picking up. seeing repeated 502s on /v1/generate in canary. tails of pod logs show OOM? or bad layers mounting. grabbing canary pod list.

ben (release): pushing new canary 3 minutes ago from pipeline. Build ID bld-2026-03-15-1420. I didn't touch image tags after manifest generation.

carmen (sre): quick diff of images in canary vs registry shows same tag but different digest. possible registry retag. command: `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood.dev/repo/model-server:canary`

anna (oncall): running verify now... output: ```
Image: registry.redwood.dev/repo/model-server:canary
Local digest: sha256:aaaa1111
Registry digest: sha256:bbbb2222
```

dinesh (platform): that digest divergence is suspicious — likely a mutable tag pushed after manifest published. canary got the old digest from cached node pool, controller pulled new digest. leads to mixed binary layer sets -> runtime errors.

anna (oncall): immediate mitigation: stop routing traffic to canary and suspend rollout. oncall runbook step 2: flip canary percent to 0 in rollout controller.

anna (oncall): `kubectl -n prod set image deploy/model-server model-server=registry.redwood.dev/repo/model-server@sha256:aaaa1111` then `kubectl rollout pause deploy/model-server`

ben (release): I'm also triggering CI job to reconcile the artifact store and re-publish a pinned digest artifact. job: `ci/release/pin-artifact:bld-2026-03-15-1420`

carmen (sre): doing quick health check after scale down -> canary error rate drops to 0. Coinbase tests pass for canary lanes now.

anna (oncall): customer impact: partial; around ~2% of production requests retried with 502s in the 10% canary cohort between 23:05-23:12 UTC. I'll update status page.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-240789-cicd-retag. severity: high, owner: anna (oncall). Add postmortem label.

dinesh (platform): root cause hypothesis: mutable tag pushed by a third-party job in the registry window between manifest generation and release promotion. this caused inconsistent pulls across nodes (some pulled new manifest layers, some had cached older layers), leading to mismatched layer sets. we'll need to scan registry event logs.

ben (release): ack. I found a failing helper that re-tagged 'canary' after a retry. disabled the helper and created fix MR to make tags immutable for release flows.

anna (oncall): anne (support) — can you check if any paying customers opened support tickets? ops-doc-bot, post note to #customer-impact with the short blurb.

ops-doc-bot: Posted: "Brief: Canary 10% saw transient 502s due to image tag retagging; traffic diverted and rollback pinned to original digest; no wide customer outage. Investigating. Follow INC-240789-cicd-retag for updates."

carmen (sre): next steps: 1) run registry audit: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=container_registry AND jsonPayload.event=TAG_PUSH" --freshness=1h` 2) verify immutability policy enforcement on registry bucket 3) schedule postmortem.

anna (oncall): handing off to night oncall (dinesh) at 00:00 UTC. summary for handoff: canary retag caused digest mismatch -> transient 502s in 10% traffic 23:05-23:12 UTC -> rollout paused and pinned to sha256:aaaa1111 -> pipeline helper disabled -> postmortem in progress.

dinesh (platform): taking handoff. I'll keep the incident assigned, continue registry audit and coordinate with release to harden CI. If anything spikes, ping me @here.

ben (release): quick Q: do we need a kill-switch feature flag for model-server image updates? we could block tag-based rollouts until pin confirmed.

carmen (sre): agree, add a preflight that validates registry digest before promotion. Add to Optimize backlog and get a hotfix for pipeline in next patch.

anna (oncall): closing the active pager. incident remains assigned to dinesh for follow-through. I'll file the incident notes and attach logs.

incident-bot: Pager closed by anna (oncall). Next update expected in postmortem doc.

dinesh (platform): leaving a final note: customers affected were small subset of API users on canary routes; no data loss. recommended actions: enforce immutable tags, add CI pinning step, and add registry write-restriction during release windows.

ben (release): will push the pipeline patch today and add gate. thanks all. :thumbsup:
